articles.title: SK Hynix shares plunge 10% amid Asia tech rout as Fed rate hike fears, AI funding worries mount
articles.summary: A sell-off in global technology hardware stocks deepened Thursday, with Asian chipmakers tracking Wall Street losses as concerns over further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, financing of artificial intelligence investments and intensifying competition weigh on sentiment. Other South Korean chip-related stocks also came under pressure.

articles.title: Oil falls as investors assess Mideast tensions, International Energy Agency's report
articles.summary: Oil fell Thursday as traders assessed potential supply disruptions following attacks on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, while digesting the International Energy Agency's latest monthly report on the outlook of the oil market. The International Energy Agency in its oil report for October out Wednesday cautioned that constraints on diesel markets could continue well into the next year, with fresh attacks on Saudi Arabia threatening to derail a recovery in oil supply.

articles.title: Anthropic's third-quarter revenue is said to hit $16.8 billion ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Anthropic told investors its third-quarter revenue stands at $16.8 billion as it prepares for a highly anticipated initial public offering reportedly slated for November, according to people familiar with the matter. The company also told investors it was cash-flow positive, generating $1.70 in revenue for every dollar spent on computing power during the third quarter, according to the Financial Times.

articles.title: Meta- and Google-backed Jio Platforms to raise up to $3.2 billion in historic IPO in India
articles.summary: Meta- and Google-backed Jio Platforms, India's largest telecom operator, is looking to raise up to 302 billion rupees ($3.2 billion) through an initial public offering of shares. Jio Platforms will sell 270 million shares in IPO priced between 1,065 rupees and 1,119 rupees apiece, from Oct. The share sale will be India's largest ever in rupee terms, but the second largest in dollar terms, marginally trailing the Hyundai Motors IPO that raised $3.3 billion in 2024.

articles.title: Bank of America hired 1,000 contractors to patch software flaws exposed by Anthropic's Mythos
articles.summary: Bank of America has hired an army of external contractors to help it patch software vulnerabilities exposed by advanced artificial intelligence models including Anthropic's Mythos, the bank's CEO, Brian Moynihan, told CNBC on Wednesday. Still, Moynihan — speaking as his company's shares slumped as much as 8% Wednesday — sought to reassure investors that the spending increase was temporary.

articles.title: How high inflation became a 'fact of life' in the U.S.
articles.summary: This yearslong spell of high inflation has cast a dark cloud over everyday Americans' view of the economy, and could shape everything from how they budget to how they vote in next month's midterm elections. All of this can make inflation a self-fulfilling prophecy, rendering the monetary policy tools at the Fed's disposal less effective in slowing price growth.

articles.title: Traders pile into 'bubble puts' on CoreWeave as neocloud stocks plunge
articles.summary: A key corner of the artificial intelligence trade is taking a beating on Wednesday and traders are betting it could get even worse. Shares of neocloud companies – businesses that offer access to the GPUs powering artificial intelligence as a service – plunged Wednesday after debt yields for Nvidia-backed CoreWeave continued to reach new heights.

Mortgage rates loosely follow the yield on the 10-year Treasury, which has been rising sharply on higher oil prices and growing concerns in the global economy.

articles.title: CoreWeave shares tumble as bond yields near 15% on concern about AI borrowing binge
articles.summary: CoreWeave's stock and bonds were both hit on Wednesday as investor fear grew that some technology companies are borrowing too heavily for the artificial intelligence build-out. While investors were once excited about getting in on the AI action, investor sentiment has started to shift, said Luis Alvarado, co-head of global fixed income strategy at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.

articles.title: BlackRock's Larry Fink warns a data center moratorium could trigger a recession
articles.summary: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink warned that a halt to data center construction could trigger an economic slowdown. "So much of our economy is based on the buildout of this capex," Fink added, referring to the massive investments made to develop artificial intelligence infrastructure. The scale of investment has created demand for construction workers, physical digital infrastructure, AI compute hardware and energy infrastructure to secure grid power, he said.
